title: Slow server start = permanently black window: 5s fallback fires, loadURL is refused, nothing retries
description: Found 2026-07-30 on the Linux desktop during MPI-391 section D, on a slow GPU-less ThinkPad. main.js:789-795 waits for the server's 'server-ready' IPC signal with a hardcoded 5000ms fallback; when it fires it calls onReady() regardless, which creates the window and calls mainWindow.loadURL('http://127.0.0.1:3000') at main.js:384. On this machine the server took ~11.6s to bind, so the load was refused with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED and the window stayed black FOREVER - there is no did-fail-load handler anywhere in main.js, so the failed load is never retried. Observed sequence in app.log/terminal: 22:21:09.668 server env injected -> '[main] Server signal timed out, attempting to create window anyway...' -> 'Failed to load URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000/ with error: ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED' -> 22:21:20.518 'App initialization started' -> 22:21:21.265 'Server started at http://127.0.0.1:3000' -> '[main] Server signaled ready.'. The server is HEALTHY the whole time; only the renderer's single load attempt failed. There is NO user-accessible recovery: Ctrl+R is not bound in the production build (confirmed live 2026-07-30), so a reload is only reachable through DevTools. The user's only option is to kill and relaunch the app, with no reason to believe that would help. ROOT FIX: add a did-fail-load handler on mainWindow.webContents that retries loadURL with backoff until the server answers - NOT simply raising the 5000ms constant, which only moves the threshold and will re-break on a slower box or a cold/AV-scanned first run. Consider also gating window creation on the real signal with a much longer safety net. Severity: a first-time user on a slow machine sees a black window and concludes the app is broken. NOT a 1.3.0 regression - the 5s fallback predates it - but it is cheap to fix and this is the first time the app has ever been launched on hardware slow enough to trip it. Windows dev PC and the SAC laptop both started under 5s, which is why it was never seen.
